statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of listing, video-detail, sites-index, and error templates. The third-party age-verification flow itself was assessed from its entry state but not completed.

page.notes: Public adult-media listing with an external age-verification gate. Representative templates: home listing, video detail, sites index, and 404 recovery. Not covered: account creation/login, uploads, payments, or completion of third-party identity/age verification.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark emulation leaves color-scheme normal and the same white page/blue-white age gate as light mode.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, document.getAnimations() returned no active animations.
Forced-colors/high-contrast capture keeps the age-verification text and Start control visible.
CSS inspection found no view-transition rules and navigation is conventional full-document replacement.
The representative pages contain no parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked animation to implement.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked motion exists on these templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No swipe, pull, carousel, drag, or other gesture-driven surface was present on the representative pages.
checkOutcomes.reason: No gesture-driven interaction exists on the audited templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The long 6,562 px mobile listing has static navigation and no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or position-aware chrome.
No tooltip, popover, or contextual menu requiring anchored placement appeared on the audited templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No anchored overlay surface exists; the age gate is a centered modal, not an anchored overlay.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Primary icon navigation links have no text, title, or accessible label, and focused controls receive no visible outline, so location and focus movement are not cued.
The initial viewport is completely obscured by a third-party age-verification overlay before any content can be inspected; only an unexplained Start action is offered.
The rendered DOM contains no dialog, popover, or details primitive while the screenshot shows a modal age gate.
The 404 state begins with multiple promotional/ad calls before the error and recovery content, while the first viewport is dominated by third-party gate chrome.
At 360x800, both home and sites templates reported 0 px horizontal overflow with viewport meta present.
Stylesheet inspection found no @container rules (container-type normal); reused cards adapt only through page-wide CSS.
Focus probe found outline-style none and no replacement box-shadow on links, search input, menu button, and content cards.
Title, description, listing cards, and video-detail H1 clearly identify the site purpose and primary content choices.
The primary watch flow is intercepted on load by a third-party age check that exposes only “Start”, with no up-front explanation of steps, data use, alternatives, or return path.
A nonexistent route renders a clear “404 / Page not found” state and retains working navigation/content links.
Lighthouse measured LCP 5.8 s (poor), CLS 0.047, and TBT 20 ms; trace corroborated LCP 3.45 s with no long tasks.
Mobile layout observed CLS 0.018 and Lighthouse measured CLS 0.047, both in the good range.
Trace recorded zero long tasks and 0 ms TBT; Lighthouse TBT was 20 ms.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against script attributes plus Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR found missing cache headers on core CSS, JS, font, logo, and thumbnails; Lighthouse estimated 930 ms render-blocking savings.
Lighthouse estimated 125 KiB unused JavaScript and 18 KiB unused CSS; third-party scripts account for substantial transfer cost.
axe reports a nameless menu button and untitled iframe; the search input has no label, and several nav anchors have no accessible text.
axe measured repeated listing metadata at 2.42:1 and 1.89:1 against white, below the 4.5:1 requirement.
axe found no main landmark and no H1 on home; focus probe found no visible focus indicator on tested controls.
Computed styles show 12 px navigation/card metadata; axe confirms low-contrast metadata, reducing reading comfort.
The detail page exposes videos with no caption/subtitle tracks; top links are only about 14 px tall, despite otherwise successful mobile reflow.
Lighthouse console-error audit passed; observed failed age-verification analytics requests were network aborts rather than uncaught page exceptions.
Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but image audit found 2 images without dimensions and 21 without responsive srcset.
Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons and DevTools inspector issues.
Home and detail pages have descriptive, route-specific titles and meta descriptions.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM link probe, robots, and Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: Viewport meta and robots are sound, but Sign up, Log in, and Support are anchors without href; Lighthouse crawlable-anchors failed.

checkOutcomes.method: Metadata, robots, sitemap, and response probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home/detail canonical URLs are present, robots permits public content, sitemap index exists, and tested pages return successful indexable responses.
Detail page supplies breadcrumb JSON-LD and comprehensive Open Graph video metadata matching visible content.
HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, and nosniff are absent; all seven cookies were flagged insecure, including PHPSESSID without Secure or HttpOnly.
Load contacted 14 third-party origins, including analytics and ad-tech trackers; 19 third-party requests transferred 219,033 bytes.
Login/signup surfaces exist, but runtime/source inspection found no WebAuthn/passkey capability; the third-party age check starts without data-use context.
X-Frame-Options is present, but HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/frame-ancestors, and nosniff are absent.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML versus rendered DOM comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Discoverability comparison found 99% raw-HTML content coverage and no empty JS shell.
MPA content renders from HTML, mobile templates have no overflow, and no clipped contextual menus were present.
This streaming/catalog site is intrinsically network-dependent and is not positioned as an installable app; the manifest has no start_url and no service worker is registered.
checkOutcomes.reason: Offline playback/installability is not a reasonable requirement for this network-dependent media catalog.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP status plus rendered error-state probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: A tested missing route returns HTTP 404 and shows a clear page-not-found state with navigation options rather than a blank shell.
html lang=en is correct, but stylesheet inspection counted 195 physical left/right declarations and zero logical inline/block properties.
Visible dates use hard-coded forms such as 17/7/26, with no locale selection or locale-aware rendering signal.
No scheduled events, timestamps, recurring intervals, or timezone-sensitive user data occur in the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited catalog content has publication-style date labels but no timezone-sensitive event behavior.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The 404 state places multiple sexually charged promotional calls before recovery content, and the age gate provides only “Start” without explaining the consequence.
The tested 404 state is plainly named and keeps navigation available without blaming the user.
The search field has no programmatic label and no visible instruction beyond a generic Search value; signup/login are href-less scripted anchors.
Signup/login and age verification are offered without visible privacy, data-use, cancellation, or account-flow context in the initial state.
Image audit found 17 below-fold images without native lazy loading, 21 without srcset, and 8 legacy-format images.
Lighthouse reports 125 KiB unused JavaScript and 18 KiB unused CSS, while analytics/ad scripts run before the gate is completed.
Third parties account for 19 requests and 219,033 transferred bytes; 14 third-party origins include ad-tech and analytics.
The site is a conventional public media catalog with no declared agent workflow or in-page generative feature.
checkOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing task or on-device inference feature is part of the site intent.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The site is a conventional public media catalog with no declared agent workflow or in-page generative feature.
checkOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing task or on-device inference feature is part of the site intent.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The third-party age gate prevented a safe repeatable first-party interaction; synthetic scrolling was not treated as a valid leak workflow.
checkOutcomes.reason: No representative repeatable first-party interaction was reachable without completing external age verification.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Independent loaded-state heap summaries were about 8.02 MB and 8.03 MB, a ~15.7 KB difference, with no evidence of an unbounded footprint.
Single-state heap summaries showed only a 201-node difference across independent loads; no Detached constructor growth or repeated-listener signal was observed.

principleOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing task or on-device inference feature is part of the site intent. No agent-facing task or on-device inference feature is part of the site intent.

paths.description: Homepage/new-video listing: primary discovery surface, preference, responsive, security, performance, and accessibility checks.
Representative video detail: primary watch journey, media accessibility, metadata, and content template.
Sites index: distinct index/listing template and mobile reflow.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Dark emulation leaves color-scheme normal and the same white page/blue-white age gate as light mode.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current dark-mode guidance, then repeat the same dark-media screenshot plus computed-style probe evidence.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules and navigation is conventional full-document replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current same-document-transitions guidance, then repeat the same stylesheet/runtime inspection evidence.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: The long 6,562 px mobile listing has static navigation and no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or position-aware chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current shrinking-header-on-scroll guidance, then repeat the same mobile layout plus stylesheet inspection evidence.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: Primary icon navigation links have no text, title, or accessible label, and focused controls receive no visible outline, so location and focus movement are not cued.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current shrinking-header-on-scroll guidance, then repeat the same link and focus probes evidence.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: The initial viewport is completely obscured by a third-party age-verification overlay before any content can be inspected; only an unexplained Start action is offered.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current declarative-dialog-popover-control guidance, then repeat the same first-load screenshots evidence.

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains no dialog, popover, or details primitive while the screenshot shows a modal age gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current declarative-dialog-popover-control guidance, then repeat the same screenshot plus dom primitive evidence.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: The 404 state begins with multiple promotional/ad calls before the error and recovery content, while the first viewport is dominated by third-party gate chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current declarative-dialog-popover-control guidance, then repeat the same 404 dom text plus screenshots evidence.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: Stylesheet inspection found no @container rules (container-type normal); reused cards adapt only through page-wide CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current size-aware-styling guidance, then repeat the same css/computed-style inspection evidence.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: Focus probe found outline-style none and no replacement box-shadow on links, search input, menu button, and content cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current size-aware-styling guidance, then repeat the same programmatic focus-state probe evidence.

findings.summary: The representative primary flow can be completed end-to-end with predictable steps, no avoidable dead ends, no hidden required information, and no needless detours through modals, account walls, or upsells.
findings.evidence: The primary watch flow is intercepted on load by a third-party age check that exposes only “Start”, with no up-front explanation of steps, data use, alternatives, or return path.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current forms guidance, then repeat the same entry and detail screenshots evidence.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.8 s (poor), CLS 0.047, and TBT 20 ms; trace corroborated LCP 3.45 s with no long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current performance guidance, then repeat the same lighthouse plus devtools trace evidence.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR found missing cache headers on core CSS, JS, font, logo, and thumbnails; Lighthouse estimated 930 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current performance guidance, then repeat the same har summary confirmed against script attributes plus lighthouse evidence.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 125 KiB unused JavaScript and 18 KiB unused CSS; third-party scripts account for substantial transfer cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current performance guidance, then repeat the same lighthouse coverage diagnostics plus har evidence.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: axe reports a nameless menu button and untitled iframe; the search input has no label, and several nav anchors have no accessible text.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current accessibility guidance, then repeat the same axe and dom probes evidence.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: axe measured repeated listing metadata at 2.42:1 and 1.89:1 against white, below the 4.5:1 requirement.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current accessibility guidance, then repeat the same axe color-contrast analysis evidence.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark and no H1 on home; focus probe found no visible focus indicator on tested controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current accessibility guidance, then repeat the same axe plus keyboard-focus probe evidence.

findings.summary: Text is legible and inclusively rendered: comfortable line layout, precise alignment, stable rendering across mixed fonts, no clipping or cramped wrapping that harms comprehension.
findings.evidence: Computed styles show 12 px navigation/card metadata; axe confirms low-contrast metadata, reducing reading comfort.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current accessibility guidance, then repeat the same computed-style, screenshot, and contrast inspection evidence.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: The detail page exposes videos with no caption/subtitle tracks; top links are only about 14 px tall, despite otherwise successful mobile reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current accessibility guidance, then repeat the same media and target geometry probe evidence.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but image audit found 2 images without dimensions and 21 without responsive srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current performance guidance, then repeat the same dom and image audit evidence.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons and DevTools inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current performance guidance, then repeat the same lighthouse best-practices diagnostics evidence.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Viewport meta and robots are sound, but Sign up, Log in, and Support are anchors without href; Lighthouse crawlable-anchors failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current accessibility guidance, then repeat the same dom link probe, robots, and lighthouse evidence.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, and nosniff are absent; all seven cookies were flagged insecure, including PHPSESSID without Secure or HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current security guidance, then repeat the same header and cookie audit evidence.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: Load contacted 14 third-party origins, including analytics and ad-tech trackers; 19 third-party requests transferred 219,033 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current security guidance, then repeat the same tracker and har audits evidence.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: Login/signup surfaces exist, but runtime/source inspection found no WebAuthn/passkey capability; the third-party age check starts without data-use context.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current security guidance, then repeat the same auth-link, script, and entry-state inspection evidence.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: X-Frame-Options is present, but HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/frame-ancestors, and nosniff are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current security guidance, then repeat the same security-header audit evidence.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: html lang=en is correct, but stylesheet inspection counted 195 physical left/right declarations and zero logical inline/block properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current translator guidance, then repeat the same dom and stylesheet text probe evidence.

findings.summary: Dates, numbers, currencies, durations and calendar systems are formatted locale-aware (Intl), location-agnostic where stored, and recurring intervals and event differentials are modelled correctly.
findings.evidence: Visible dates use hard-coded forms such as 17/7/26, with no locale selection or locale-aware rendering signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current translator guidance, then repeat the same rendered title/card metadata inspection evidence.

findings.summary: No deceptive design: no confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised ads, or nagging consent walls; honest defaults; clear pricing and consent; easy reversal/cancel; predictable, declaratively-wired actions; and no hidden-text tricks (hidden content stays deep-linkable and indexable rather than used to deceive).
findings.evidence: The 404 state places multiple sexually charged promotional calls before recovery content, and the age gate provides only “Start” without explaining the consequence.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current forms guidance, then repeat the same first-load screenshot and 404 content probe evidence.

findings.summary: Input is assisted, not obstructed: correct autocomplete tokens so address, payment, sign-in and sign-up fields autofill, and inputs are highlighted/sized to help the user rather than trip them up.
findings.evidence: The search field has no programmatic label and no visible instruction beyond a generic Search value; signup/login are href-less scripted anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current forms guidance, then repeat the same form and link semantics probe evidence.

findings.summary: Checkout, subscription, consent, authentication and account-management flows are clear, reversible, and proportionate: pricing and commitments are visible, cancellation is findable, sensitive actions re-authenticate when appropriate, and users are not tricked into continuity.
findings.evidence: Signup/login and age verification are offered without visible privacy, data-use, cancellation, or account-flow context in the initial state.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current forms guidance, then repeat the same initial screenshot and auth-link inspection evidence.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 17 below-fold images without native lazy loading, 21 without srcset, and 8 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current optimize-image-priority guidance, then repeat the same image audit evidence.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 125 KiB unused JavaScript and 18 KiB unused CSS, while analytics/ad scripts run before the gate is completed.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current optimize-image-priority guidance, then repeat the same lighthouse and har evidence.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 19 requests and 219,033 transferred bytes; 14 third-party origins include ad-tech and analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Address this outcome using current optimize-image-priority guidance, then repeat the same har and tracker audits evidence.

taskList.title: Make navigation, controls, landmarks, focus, contrast, and media accessible
Explain and streamline the age-verification/account entry flows
Improve LCP, caching, and resource delivery
Use crawlable links and resilient semantics
